A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between appendices C and D.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments comparing voting and debate, intervention experiments, and additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Sparse MAD continuation results on Formal Logic in Appendix E, Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: The debate procedures, Bayesian update model, MAD-oracle, MAD-Conformist and MAD-Follower remain unchanged. Section 2's explicit inclusion of an agent's own response clarifies behavior already documented in v1's Appendix B.1 prompt.

E1.justification: The seven question-answering/alignment benchmarks and CNN/DailyMail summarization are retained. The new diagnostic reuses Formal Logic, existing models and Sparse MAD; the added line-graph and ring-graph counterexamples are theoretical.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same single-agent, Majority Voting, Decentralized MAD, Sparse MAD, Centralized MAD and intervention methods. The new continuation diagnostic does not add or remove a comparator from an existing comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a conditional-continuation evaluation: previous-round mean agent accuracy is compared with estimated next-round accuracy over three Sparse MAD rounds for two models on Formal Logic. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, sampling settings and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 supports martingale behavior through mean-accuracy trajectories. v2 adds a targeted diagnostic in Tables 7–8 examining approximate conditional-mean preservation for Sparse MAD, whose topology lacks the general theoretical guarantee. Existing agent-count and answer-extraction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports five independent next-round continuations to estimate conditional expectations in the new diagnostic, distinct from the retained five-run single-agent averages. Tables 7–8 include parenthesized quantities without defining their statistical meaning. No increase in repetitions for existing experiments is stated.

E6.justification: New Tables 7–8 add three rounds of diagnostic results per model. For example, round 1 compares 0.363 with an estimated next-round 0.386 for Qwen and 0.451 with 0.446 for Llama. All pre-existing tabulated scores are retained; these are additional results, not revised benchmark performance.

T1.justification: Theorem 2 explicitly incorporates the neighbor-average belief condition previously derived at the end of v1's Appendix C.3, with a revised proof and filtration. New material establishes sufficient topologies, supplies line/ring counterexamples, and derives a collective-belief martingale for fully connected heterogeneous agents with equal belief-vector totals. Theorem 1.A is relocated rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: voting explains most gains, debate admits a martingale characterization, and correctness-preserving interventions improve debate. Their wording does not incorporate the new detailed theoretical qualifications.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops the applicability boundaries of its central martingale interpretation. It identifies supported topologies, explicitly explains why Sparse MAD's ring lacks a guarantee, and conjectures approximate behavior over short debates. It also distinguishes heterogeneous collective-belief preservation from individual-belief preservation, extending beyond v1's brief consistency assumption.

D1.justification: Table 6's caption newly identifies the Figure 4 results as fully connected Decentralized MAD. This is additional documentation, not evidence of a changed setting. Sampling hyperparameters, hardware, dataset-processing descriptions, prompts and the code-access URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, contribution positioning and 46 referenced works are retained. Added appendix citations reuse existing sources to identify the analyzed debate architectures.

P1.justification: Appendices C and D exchange order, the martingale proof is reorganized, and Broader Impact moves to Appendix H. There are localized explanatory edits, an author-name change and an updated conference footer; most existing prose and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two compact diagnostic tables and simple line/ring topology diagrams, expands Table 6's caption, and adjusts surrounding layout. Existing main figures and table structures are retained. v1's Tables 7–8 become v2's Tables 9–10 without result changes.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical precision by making a condition already present in v1's proof explicit in Theorem 2 and explaining valid and invalid topologies. The collective-belief extension and focused continuation diagnostic add useful support. The net gain is limited by retained broad abstract/conclusion claims and the diagnostic's narrow coverage and undefined parenthesized uncertainty quantities.
